heard: Out of a trillion photons, only one makes it through this cloud. In 1919, American astronomer Edward Emerson Barnard first cataloged this mysterious, ink-black, gaping void in the night sky. Floating deep in the southern constellation Ophiuchus, this dense-bock globule spans fully half a lightyear across. It sits roughly 400 lightyears away from Earth, and not a single foreground star pierces its absolute, ink-black darkness. Inside, temperatures plummet to approximately 10 Kelvin, colder than Pluto, causing gases to freeze solid onto floating dust grains. Astronomers discovered this starless stellar nursery is currently vibrating like Jell-O, preparing to collapse and birth a brand new star. It creates a perfect hole in the sky, but this shadow is made of solid cold cosmic dust.
